title: The Errand
summary: Carrie arrives with one DTI errand while the household is already eating breakfast; Gunnar treats the appointment as a route to learn, not a mystery to worship.
panelPlan: Wide: Morning in the Safe Cave. Astrid and the two male Kin remain together around breakfast and simple household tasks while Carrie puts an appointment slip and two MetroCards on the table.
Medium: Gunnar reads the numbered address and transit line without touching the cards.
Medium: Bjorn finishes coffee.
Wide: The three Kin continue breakfast rather than preparing to follow.
Close: Gunnar pockets one MetroCard.

title: The Key Stays Home
summary: Before leaving, Bjorn gives Astrid the apartment key, a small sign that the household already exists independently of the two men Carrie usually takes into the city.
settingText: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hall
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn reaches for the brass key, then looks back at Astrid and the two male Kin staying in 5B.
Close: He places the key in Astrid's palm.
Medium: Astrid closes her hand around it without ceremony.
Wide: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar step into the hall while the three Kin remain together inside.
Close: Carrie notices the handoff but does not comment.

title: Burial Road
summary: The subway entrance is still intimidating, but Gunnar responds by watching people use it rather than turning the threshold into a refusal.
panelPlan: Wide: The trio stops above the subway stairs as commuters move around them.
Medium: Bjorn looks down into the station.
Close: Gunnar watches three unrelated commuters descend without hesitation.
Medium: A commuter brushes past with a coffee and disappears underground.
Two-shot: Gunnar starts down.

title: The Gate Refuses Her
summary: Carrie's demonstration fails, making room for Gunnar to learn by watching rather than for the issue to spend pages explaining transit technology.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie takes one MetroCard and demonstrates a confident swipe.
Insert: The turnstile flashes rejection.
Medium: An impatient commuter gestures without stopping.
Close: Bjorn looks at Carrie.
Medium: Carrie flips the card and tries again.

title: Gunnar Reads the Swipe
summary: Gunnar solves the turnstile by observing commuter rhythm and body mechanics, establishing his adaptation as practical pattern reading rather than magic-system decoding.
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar steps aside and silently watches several commuters swipe and push through.
Close: His attention follows card angle, hand speed and the timing of pressure against the bar.
Medium: He swipes once and passes cleanly.
Medium: Carrie stares.
Two-shot: Bjorn takes the card from Gunnar.

title: The Iron Worm Arrives
summary: The first train arrival is allowed to be frightening and physical, then immediately ordinary because New Yorkers simply board it.
panelPlan: Wide: A train roars into the station; Bjorn braces instinctively while Gunnar tracks the braking lights and door positions.
Medium: The train stops exactly where commuters expected.
Wide: Doors open and people exit around Bjorn without acknowledging his stance.
Medium: Gunnar steps aboard first, eyes on the route strip above the doors.
Close: Bjorn follows.

title: Crowd Without Banners
summary: Inside the train, Bjorn begins learning that dense public space has rules nobody announces, while Gunnar watches how riders create room for one another without command.
panelPlan: Wide: Packed train car. Bjorn occupies too much doorway space until the crowd naturally routes around him.
Medium: Carrie gently pulls him one step away from the doors.
Close: Gunnar watches a rider fold inward to let a stroller pass.
Medium: Bjorn copies the movement when another passenger needs the pole.
Wide: The train leaves the station with all three embedded in ordinary commuter life.

dialogueInline.text: They don't wait for the doors to clear.

title: The Busker
summary: A busker turns the trip into the first moment of warmth with a stranger, giving Bjorn a social encounter that is not about failing a system.
panelPlan: Medium: A busker finishes a song in the car or on the platform and passes a small container for tips.
Close: Bjorn listens with unexpected seriousness.
Medium: Carrie drops a dollar in the container.
Two-shot: Bjorn nods solemnly to the busker.
Close: Gunnar smiles at Bjorn rather than at the modern object.

dialogueInline.text: Tip him if you mean it.

title: Between Stations
summary: Carrie's work problem changes the route while Gunnar is already learning station order, showing that useful navigation grows inside an ordinary conversation rather than from a puzzle page.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie's phone buzzes. She answers while Gunnar follows station names above the door.
Medium: DTI supervisor voice through phone.
Close: Carrie closes her eyes.
Medium: Gunnar points to the next transfer stop on the route strip.
Two-shot: Carrie checks her phone map, then looks at him.

dialogueInline.text: The annex function moved. Your appointment is at the temporary office.

title: Above Ground
summary: The trio emerges into an unfamiliar part of the city and Gunnar orients from physical cues while Carrie is still fighting the updated address on her phone.
settingText: Midtown or downtown street near the temporary DTI annex
panelPlan: Wide: They come up a different subway exit into a dense avenue with trucks, scaffolding and cross traffic.
Medium: Carrie rotates her phone trying to match the moved annex address.
Close: Gunnar looks at the sun angle, numbered cross street and flow of traffic rather than her screen.
Medium: He points one block over.
Two-shot: Bjorn starts walking with Gunnar.

dialogueInline.text: My phone says west. That's not west.

title: Lunch Window
summary: A short food stop lets Bjorn and Gunnar experience the city between destinations, and Carrie's repeated small expenditures quietly continue Bjorn's discomfort with dependence.
settingText: Street food cart / sidewalk near DTI annex
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie stops at a hotdog cart because the appointment was pushed and nobody has eaten since morning.
Medium: The vendor hands over three hotdogs while Bjorn watches Carrie pay.
Medium: Gunnar studies the cart's small ecosystem: vendor, regular customer, delivery bike, condiment bottles.
Close: Bjorn takes one bite and decides the food is acceptable.
Medium: The vendor has already moved on to the next customer.

title: Nothing Useful
summary: Gunnar spends a few minutes watching city life without mapping it, the first explicit hint that his attention may become personal curiosity rather than permanent navigation duty.
settingText: Small public seating area near the annex
panelPlan: Wide: The trio sits on a low wall or small public bench finishing lunch while pedestrians cross the frame.
Medium: Gunnar watches a dog refuse to move, a cyclist lock up, and office workers argue over coffee.
Two-shot: Bjorn notices Gunnar has no map, paper or transit card in his hands.
Close: Gunnar keeps watching the street.
Medium: Carrie hears the answer and, for once, does not give them another instruction.

title: The House Hides Its Name
summary: The moved annex is difficult to identify and its posted directions contradict one another, but Gunnar solves the problem by watching the route employees actually use.
settingText: Temporary DTI annex exterior and side entrance
panelPlan: Wide: Plain temporary municipal office exterior with a small DTI paper sign taped behind glass and older building signage still visible.
Medium: Bjorn compares the appointment slip with the nearly hidden sign.
Medium: Carrie finds a front-door notice pointing to SIDE ENTRANCE and then a side-door notice pointing back toward reception.
Two-shot: Bjorn looks between the conflicting notices.
Close: Gunnar watches an employee carrying coffee use an unmarked working service door.
Medium: Carrie follows his gaze.

dialogueInline.text: Front says side. Side says front.

title: The Hidden Hall
summary: Carrie reluctantly follows the route staff actually use, while Bjorn recognizes the invisible labor infrastructure underneath an institution that looks confusing from the front.
settingText: DTI annex service entrance and interior corridor
panelPlan: Wide: The three enter through the working service door alongside a maintenance worker with a cart.
Medium: Gunnar holds the door for the worker rather than blocking it.
Medium: Bjorn looks at supply carts, taped arrows and employee doors.
Medium: Carrie points down a corridor marked RECEPTION.
Wide: They move with staff flow rather than wandering deeper.

dialogueInline.text: So this is how staff come through.

title: Reception
summary: The remaining bureaucratic comedy is compressed into one reception beat: the original-copy contradiction, chained pen, and required sign-in all happen at the same desk.
panelPlan: Wide: Plain reception desk with paper sign-in sheet, chained blue pen and stacks of moved-office folders.
Medium: Bjorn looks at the chained pen.
Medium: Carrie presents the housing confirmation.
Medium: Receptionist inspects it.
Close: Gunnar watches the stamp pad beside the clerk.

dialogueInline.text: I need the original marked original.

title: The Stamp
summary: The actual errand ends quickly once they reach the right desk, deliberately refusing to let the institution occupy the final third of the issue.
panelPlan: Insert: The receptionist stamps the housing confirmation.
Medium: Carrie looks at the now-completed page.
Medium: Gunnar waits for the next instruction.
Two-shot: Bjorn looks toward the exit.
Wide: They leave the desk while another ordinary case is already moving into their place.

dialogueInline.text: We came all this way for a stamp.

title: Do We Have to Go Home?
summary: With the required task complete, Gunnar asks whether travel can include a choice that serves no administrative purpose.
panelPlan: Wide: Outside, Carrie folds the stamped confirmation into her folder and starts toward the subway.
Medium: Gunnar stays where he is for one beat.
Close: Carrie looks at him, unsure what problem he has found.
Medium: Gunnar points toward a side street he noticed earlier.
Two-shot: Bjorn studies him, then starts in that direction.

dialogueInline.text: Do we have to go straight back?
I want to see what's over there.

title: One Block Wrong on Purpose
summary: Gunnar deliberately takes a route that is unnecessary, converting navigation from survival skill into personal curiosity.
settingText: Ordinary city side street and small public plaza
panelPlan: Wide: The trio walks one block off the efficient route into a small plaza with trees, food workers on break, parents, bikes and a public sculpture.
Medium: Gunnar slows to look at the sculpture and the people using the square around it.
Medium: Carrie checks the time and almost speaks, then puts her phone away.
Two-shot: Bjorn looks back toward the subway entrance they passed.
Close: Gunnar smiles slightly.

title: Five Minutes
summary: Carrie allows the day to contain five purposeless minutes, and the three begin to feel less like caseworker plus assignment and more like people sharing time.
panelPlan: Wide: They sit on a public bench. Gunnar watches the square; Bjorn people-watches; Carrie has the folder closed beside her.
Medium: A work notification lights Carrie's phone. She silences it without opening the message.
Two-shot: Bjorn notices.
Medium: Gunnar watches a child chase a pigeon across the square and says nothing.
Wide: For one panel nobody is solving anything.

title: Get Us Home
summary: Carrie hands Gunnar the return journey, turning his accumulated observation into responsibility rather than a trick he performs for approval.
panelPlan: Wide: They stand at the subway entrance after the break.
Medium: Carrie holds out the two MetroCards toward Gunnar.
Close: Gunnar takes them without looking surprised.
Medium: Bjorn steps toward the stairs.
Wide: Gunnar goes first.

title: The Transfer
summary: A real service change tests Gunnar once, and he solves it from physical traces and commuter behavior rather than requiring several pages of transit exposition.
panelPlan: Wide: At a transfer junction, a temporary service notice redirects one line while an older arrow remains visible underneath.
Medium: Carrie starts to open her phone.
Close: Gunnar studies the exposed older arrow, yellow tape and the direction most commuters are taking.
Medium: He points down a corridor.
Two-shot: Carrie checks the sign, then follows.

dialogueInline.text: Old arrow under the tape. People are still turning here.

title: Different Stair
summary: Gunnar chooses a different station exit from the one they used that morning and proves he is navigating the neighborhood rather than memorizing a single route.
panelPlan: Wide: They emerge from a different Bushwick staircase into late-afternoon neighborhood light.
Medium: Gunnar points down the block toward familiar storefronts.
Medium: Carrie recognizes the bodega awning in the distance.
Close: Gunnar looks pleased without performing triumph.

title: The Block Opens Home
summary: The return route resolves into ordinary neighborhood recognition and then into the household itself when Astrid opens 5B with the key Bjorn left her.
settingText: Bushwick neighborhood sidewalk and fifth-floor hallway outside apartment 5B
panelPlan: Wide: The trio walks past the familiar bodega and apartment block in late-afternoon light; Gunnar checks no map.
Medium: Bjorn looks toward the bodega.
Wide: They climb the familiar building stairs and stop at 5B.
Medium: Bjorn knocks once. Astrid opens the door with the brass key still in hand; the two male Kin are visible behind her.
Medium: Bjorn steps inside.
Wide: Carrie enters last carrying the stamped confirmation while Gunnar pauses at the threshold, looking from the hall he navigated back to the room he returned to.

dialogueInline.text: We still owe the downstairs man.

title: I Brought Us Back
summary: Gunnar claims the return as his achievement while the issue lands on household continuity, not transit mastery for its own sake.
panelPlan: Wide: The household resumes around them: food on the table, bedding, key back on its hook, the stamped DTI paper set aside near Carrie's folder.
Medium: Bjorn takes off his coat.
Medium: Gunnar sets the MetroCards beside the household map, then looks at Bjorn.
Close: Gunnar allows himself the distinction.
Medium: Carrie hears it while Astrid begins serving food.

dialogueInline.text: Train got us most of the way.
